notes.title: MYCELIUM HEAVEN DEVLOG #2 - LOGO AND KEY ART
notes.notes:
Hello, hello Indiedev, Indiegame and Mushroom lovers! 🤠

Today, we’ll be discussing the evolution of *Mycelium Heaven*'s logo and key art.
So, first things first. Behold, the first Itch thumbnail:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44709654/ca245f2cba8323d0802330920043c614cd4c90ac.png[/img]

Outstanding, I know. Just keep in mind that this was made for a game jam, and I was working solo. I left the capsule and title for the very last minute. In the Unreal Editor, the game was titled *Juego Setas* ("Mushroom Game") and *No hay mal que por bien no venga* ("There's always a silver lining") on the Notion page.
I even used this rough version of the logo to pitch the game for a while, but thankfully, that didn’t last long. My dad came to the rescue.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44709654/2726a54116e24827c473606d7e5770c655268ba5.png[/img]

One evening at my grandparents' house, we came up with a new logo. My dad sketched it, and I colored it. So, big thanks to my dad [url=https://raulocaceres.es/][b](Raúlo Cáceres)[/b][/url] for his time and to my mom for being there to capture the moment.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44709654/e94a45a7d0c44d7bffab576ed56a8007a4a360c7.png[/img]

This was the main capsule for a while. But then I joined Dojo System! And they helped me a lot with some polishing deteails, like changing thar logo for a new one.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44709654/9fa1591597814ca436192e446fa33b91ab36d825.png[/img]

Now that’s a pretty cool-looking video game title, if you ask me. And you know what would be even cooler? An illustration!

[previewyoutube=ZvtRL3r1-Yw;full][/previewyoutube]
And this super awesome cover art has been made by 
[url=https://www.instagram.com/molluar_dawson/profilecard/?igsh=YnJidXhtN3Q3ajhn][b]Azul Fernández[/b][/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44709654/bd4e94695b22b93d5567d7709a283a47807d8bc7.png[/img]

I think this new look fits the game perfectly. Spooky, fun, intriguing, and full of mushrooms!
See you in the next one!👋

notes.title: MYCELIUM HEAVEN DEVLOG #2 - PROGRAMACIÓN
notes.notes:
[b]MYCELIUM HEAVEN DEVLOG #2 - PROGRAMMING[/b]

Hey there, Indie Game lovers, strategy game fans, and mushroom enthusiasts! 🌱

Today, I’m here to talk a bit about the programming in Mycelium Heaven.

Just a disclaimer: programming isn’t exactly my passion. I code because the game needs to do stuff. Maybe that's why I ended up making the game in:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44709654/192f8c5ff0897e265987c53b9bba8f36a1fa6174.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44709654/4a4c5e647ee76704453f59e21d122808cd587beb.png[/img]

In general, there isn’t much to comment on; most of the logic load is on the main character and the tiles, which have functions the character can call.

I should mention I didn’t put much thought into class structure or anything because the game started from a jam. I had more coffee in my veins than hours of sleep. Thankfully, I had a lightbulb moment and decided to use inheritance for the tiles, because systems ended up in the final game that, honestly, I wouldn’t implement the same way now. But I think that’s part of the beauty of watching projects evolve—you learn what’s scalable and what’s not.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44709654/233aca98d2569c332dfcf062c260d56563c61cb5.png[/img]

I’ll end with this special shout-out to a comment I left during a desperate moment trying to fix a bug:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44709654/c426559d08172bd70fb35f7a5add42745e55dcc9.png[/img]

I think I mentioned it was a bad move to do a get all of class and then cast, but hey, the bug got fixed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44709654/810dca68dffcbb37f1250d19a83a0fa2dd430ce0.png[/img]

See you in the next one! 👋

notes.title: MYCELIUM HEAVEN DEVLOG #1 - ART
notes.notes:
[h1]MYCELIUM HEAVEN DEVLOG #1 - ARTE[/h1]
 
Hiii!
    
Today we are going to talk about Mycelium Heaven’s art.
    
[h2]🌲Why?⏰[/h2]
    
I knew I wanted to make the style 3D and low poly so I could produce the assets in a reasonable amount of time with a distinct look. I really like heavily textured, stylized 3D games, so I took inspiration from "Shelter".
    
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44709654/56d323d456225a56d3c6df3fa9788649424d723d.png[/img]
    
I don’t usually work with sketches, and since this game was made for a Jam, to see what I wanted to do first I just opened Blender, made some cute low poly models, and then jumped to Substance Painter to give them the final look. After a bit of trial and error, I arrived at some textures that I liked. Then I just made the rest of the assets to match the look.

One thing that I was aming for is that a frame from my game needed to be distinct enough to be recognisble. I like it when you see a screenshot and you can inmediately say “hey, that’s from that game”.
    
[h2]🖥️How?🖱️[/h2]
    
My asset-making pipeline is basically this:

First, I look for references. Sometimes they go on a Notion page; most of the time, they are a few tabs open in my browser.
    
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44709654/63200343f625df327a1bcfb8083cdeedd723000f.png[/img]
    
Then I make a little drawing in a notebook (a very optional step).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44709654/e91bfaf6f40e3e91037a7526ef209365af0177f2.jpg[/img]

After that, I make a 3D version of it in Blender, trying to stick to the level of low-poly that I have established. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44709654/cfbca8eab8784908408c2834d6b6ecfc06f767b2.png[/img]

A very important step here is to vertex paint the different parts of the model so I can apply different colors and patterns more easily later. 
    
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44709654/5f927f7c1b7d32e95a0b5fb1cecd334a99eca4eb.png[/img]
    
Finally I go to Substance Painter and give it some life. I use the vertex color as a color ID map to create masks and apply color more easily.

Here is where I usually experiment the most and try different looks. Most of what I do is based on basic colors and patterns, so iterating is quite fast.
    
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44709654/4f13cf75c23065f240572d7a157d6f83ed787ee6.png[/img]
    
And when it’s done, the model and the texture (yes, the entire game is made only with base colors, I really like the plastic look) goes to Unreal, and it’s ready to go.
    
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44709654/ba4171d9e8b2c8319cd87a076b3d43b244f5f81b.png[/img]
    
I hope you enjoyed my little rambling about game art!

See you in the next one 😉

notes.title: Alpha 1.4.1 Update
notes.notes:
Hi !🙆‍♂️🧙‍♂️

Once again, all of the feedback is being super useful, so thank you very much 🤗. I want the game to be as readable as possible because the challenge has to come from the puzzles, not from not knowing what's going on.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44709654/51187d9d7f55581f7cde9b2aed521ada9a47eee6.png[/img]
Here is a little list of what changed:

[list]
[*] [b]Tiles now have a border![/b]
   - Active tiles have a thick border so you don't depend on brightness only to see them. The contrast of the basic tile has been increased, and a new thinner border added so they stand out more on every floor.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44709654/548317ae8ac87ed1255dcb4086b9834e48ed7cfb.gif[/img]
[*] [b]Easier to read graves[/b]
   - Numbers on graves now have a white border. They are also a little bit tilted to face the camera.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44709654/974696f2819dec80136b687ceb4c66ad53ade9bf.png[/img]
[*] [b]Meet Obo🎃[/b]
   - The first easter egg! If you say hi to our dumb little friend in the menu; he will jiggle and bounce.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44709654/27f7378d3a31bbf8530e074e8ba47ec3b9d07c64.gif[/img]
[/list]

I have also been working on getting the game in the Play Store, and it was hard but things are working out! I'm going to start making the two new seasons soon, so this is probably the last demo update. 
We'll see each other when the game releases, but if you want to keep up with every little thing going on in the development (I might have an oversharing problem), you can tag along on [url=https://twitter.com/3DGoblinDev]X[/url] or [url=tiktok.com/@3dgoblindev]TikTok [/url](@3DGoblinDev).

Take care and have a nice holiday season! 🤙
